quick: Oral suspension 800 mg/day (20 mL) for AIDS-related anorexia/cachexia
May be taken without regard to meals; shake suspension well
Metabolism may be affected; use caution
Weight, blood glucose, adrenal function, thromboembolism signs
summary: Megestrol acetate is a synthetic progestin. The oral suspension is indicated for anorexia, cachexia or significant unexplained weight loss in patients with AIDS, given at 800 mg/day. By an incompletely understood mechanism it stimulates appetite and weight gain. Important concerns include glucocorticoid-like effects (new-onset or worsened diabetes, Cushingoid features, and adrenal suppression/insufficiency on withdrawal), thromboembolic disease, and fetal harm. It is contraindicated in pregnancy and should be reserved for patients in whom treatable causes of weight loss have been addressed.
indications: Treatment of anorexia, cachexia, or an unexplained significant weight loss in patients with a diagnosis of acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS)

dosage.n: 400 and 800 mg/day both shown effective; shake well before use

admin: Shake the oral suspension well before measuring each dose
Institute therapy only after treatable causes of weight loss (malignancy, infection, malabsorption, endocrine, renal, psychiatric) are sought and addressed
Not intended for prophylactic use to prevent weight loss
Use with caution in patients with a history of thromboembolic disease
Consider adrenal-axis effects when starting, and especially when stopping, chronic therapy
moa: Megestrol acetate is a synthetic derivative of progesterone with antiestrogenic and glucocorticoid-like activity. The precise mechanism by which it stimulates appetite and produces weight gain in anorexia/cachexia is unknown but is thought to involve central appetite stimulation and metabolic effects. In hormone-sensitive tumors it exerts antineoplastic progestational effects.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to megestrol acetate or any component
relative: Patients at risk of adrenal insufficiency (especially on withdrawal)
monitor: Signs of adrenal insufficiency / Cushing's syndrome

preg: Contraindicated. Megestrol may cause fetal harm; there are no adequate well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Women of childbearing potential should avoid pregnancy and use contraception during therapy; if pregnancy occurs, advise of the potential hazard to the fetus.
lact: Breastfeeding is not recommended during megestrol therapy because of the potential for serious adverse effects in the infant (and HIV transmission risk in the indicated population).
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is provided for renal impairment.
hepatic: Plasma levels depend partly on hepatic inactivation; use with caution in hepatic impairment.

major: Warfarin - megestrol may increase INR; monitor closely
moderate: Drugs affecting glucose control - additive hyperglycemia; adjust antidiabetic therapy
Corticosteroids - additive glucocorticoid effects / adrenal suppression
minor: No significant change in zidovudine or rifabutin pharmacokinetics requiring adjustment
interactions.food: May be taken without regard to meals; shake suspension well.
interactions.diagnostics: May raise blood glucose, alter adrenal-axis (ACTH stimulation) testing, and increase INR with warfarin.

serious: Adrenal insufficiency (during therapy or on withdrawal)
emergency: Pulmonary embolism / DVT (chest pain, dyspnea, leg swelling)
Adrenal crisis (hypotension, vomiting, weakness) on withdrawal

monitoring: Clinical signs of adrenal insufficiency or Cushing's syndrome (especially when starting or stopping)
counsel: Shake the bottle well before each dose
This medicine is to help your appetite and weight - take it as directed
If you are able to become pregnant, use contraception and tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant
Report leg swelling/pain, chest pain or breathlessness, and increased thirst/urination (high blood sugar)
Do not stop the medicine suddenly after long-term use without medical advice, because of effects on your adrenal glands
pk: Appetite/weight effects develop over weeks of therapy
Variable; dependent on assay and gut/hepatic inactivation
Store at 20-25 C; dispense in a tight container; protect from heat
pearls: Has glucocorticoid activity - can cause new diabetes, Cushingoid features, and adrenal suppression with insufficiency on withdrawal
Increases thromboembolic risk - use caution with prior VTE
Reserve for AIDS-related anorexia/cachexia after treatable causes are addressed; not for prophylaxis
May raise INR in patients on warfarin
Contraceptive use is advised; contraindicated in pregnancy
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your schedule - do not double the dose.
overdose: No serious unexpected effects occurred at doses up to 1200 mg/day; reported overdose effects include diarrhea, nausea, abdominal pain, dyspnea, cough, unsteady gait and chest pain. There is no specific antidote - provide supportive care. Dialysis is unlikely to be effective because of low solubility.
